title: Conservation of Mass and Balanced Equations Assessment
description: Checkpoint assessment for mass conservation, atom counting, and explaining why chemical equations must balance.

questions.question: A reaction takes place in a sealed container. The reactants have a total mass of 25 g. What should be the total mass of the products?
questions.explanation: In a sealed or closed container, mass is conserved, so the products must have the same total mass as the reactants.

questions.question: Which statement explains why products can be new substances even though atoms are conserved?
options: The atoms are rearranged into different combinations.
The old atoms are destroyed and replaced.
questions.explanation: New substances form when the same atoms are connected and arranged in new ways.

questions.question: If an equation is balanced, each element has the same number of atoms on the reactant side and product side.
questions.explanation: Balancing requires matching the atom count for every element across the arrow.

questions.question: Which equation is balanced?
questions.explanation: 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO has 2 Mg atoms and 2 O atoms on both sides.

questions.question: Count the oxygen atoms on the product side of CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O.
questions.explanation: CO2 has 2 oxygen atoms, and 2H2O has 2 more oxygen atoms. The product side has 4 oxygen atoms total.

questions.question: In a closed system, 15 g of reactant A combines with 20 g of reactant B. The total mass of products is ____ g.
questions.explanation: Add the reactant masses: 15 g + 20 g = 35 g.

questions.question: Balancing a chemical equation should be done by changing subscripts inside correct chemical formulas.
questions.explanation: Balancing is done by changing coefficients. Subscripts are part of a substance's formula and changing them changes the substance.

questions.question: The equation H2 + O2 -> H2O is not balanced because:
options: The arrow points the wrong way.
questions.explanation: The reactant side has 2 oxygen atoms in O2, but the product side has only 1 oxygen atom in H2O.

questions.question: Fill in the coefficient that balances the product side: 2H2 + O2 -> ____H2O.
questions.explanation: Placing 2 before H2O gives 4 H atoms and 2 O atoms on the product side, matching the reactants.

questions.question: A student heats a substance in an open beaker and finds less mass afterward. Which explanation best fits conservation of mass?
options: The law of conservation of mass stopped working.
Some matter may have escaped as a gas.
The missing mass turned into nothing.
questions.explanation: In an open container, gas can escape. The law is clearest when all matter is kept in a closed system.

questions.question: Explain why 2Na + Cl2 -> 2NaCl is balanced.
questions.correctAnswer: It is balanced because both sides have 2 sodium atoms and 2 chlorine atoms. The atoms are rearranged into sodium chloride, but the counts stay the same.
questions.explanation: A correct explanation names the atom counts for Na and Cl on both sides.

questions.question: A student writes C + O2 -> CO and says it is balanced because there is one carbon atom on each side. Explain the error.
questions.correctAnswer: The student counted carbon but ignored oxygen. The reactant side has 2 oxygen atoms in O2, while CO has only 1 oxygen atom, so the equation is not balanced.
questions.explanation: Every element must be counted. Matching only one element is not enough to prove an equation is balanced.
